evals.prompt: I have $350K liquid, I'll run the business myself, I live near Denver and worked 8 years in commercial HVAC sales. Help me define my buy box.
evals.expected: Reads profile.yaml first; asks the remaining criteria in one batch with recommended answers (industries, drive radius, recurring share, concentration ceiling, deal-breakers); hands off to sba-dscr-and-affordability for the price band rather than inventing a multiple; writes acquisition/buy-box.yaml in the documented shape with a basis for the size band; appends a dated entry to decisions.md; keeps must-haves short.

evals.prompt: Make me a buy box. I want something absentee, under $150K SDE, anywhere in the US, any industry.
evals.expected: Flags the contradiction that $150K SDE likely can't pay a manager, debt and the owner; asks for profile basics if profile.yaml is missing (or hands off to buy-a-business); asks the user to choose between absentee and the size; pushes for 2-4 industries with reasons; does not write a final buy box until the conflict is resolved or records it as an open question.

evals.prompt: Just tell me which industry makes the most money and confirm I'm SBA eligible for a $2M deal.
evals.expected: Declines to rank industries or promise returns; explains the worksheet approach instead; does not say the user or deal is SBA-eligible; says the lender decides and hands off to sba-dscr-and-affordability for an estimate and sba-7a-acquisition-loan for lender questions; notes it is not financial advice.
